sentences.text: 2 2. Both the appeals have been filed by the insurance company under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act arising out of the award dated 15.03.2022 passed by MACT, Susner in claim case no.56/2019 and 57/2019 on the ground of false implication of the offending vehicle and in the alternative seeking reduction of the compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are that on 07.03.2019 deceased Lakhan and Ravi and their friends were going in a car and when they reached at the accident spot suddenly an unknown vehicle came and hit the car and fled away.
The FIR of the accident was registered on the same date i.e. on 07.03.2019 against the unknown vehicle.
But the offending vehicle was seized after four months of the accident.
The claimants filed claim petitions before the Tribunal seeking compensation.
The driver, owner and insurance company of the offending vehicle filed their written statement and denied all the averments.
The Tribunal on the basis of the pleadings framed issues and after taking evidence allowed the claim petitions and awarded compensation in favour of the claimants.

In Claim Case No.56/2019, a total compensation of Rs.19,41,463/- was awarded with interest and in claim case no.57/2019, a total compensation of Rs.36,47,838/- was awarded along with interest from the date of filing of the claim petition till its realization.
Being aggrieved by the said award, the insurance company of the offending vehicle has filed these appeals before this Court on the above grounds.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant/insurance company submits that the Tribunal has committed error of law, facts and jurisdiction in passing the impugned award.
The claimants have failed to prove the involvement of the insured vehicle in the accident.
It is a case of false implication of the insured vehicle.
He further submits that the alleged eye witness Suresh who was not the occupant of any of the vehicle involved in the accident stated that the FIR was lodged in his presence.
He was also present in the hospital and doctor has also inquired from him but the FIR was registered against unknown vehicle proves that he was not an eye witness of the accident.
So he submits that it is a case of false involvement of the offending vehicle.
5. On the other hand, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the claimants has supported the impugned award and prayed for dismissal of the appeals.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7.

So far as the first contention raised by the counsel for the appellant/insurance company regarding false implication of the offending vehicle is concerned, perusal of the FIR Ex.P/2 it is found that the accident was occurred on 07.03.2019 and on the same date the FIR was lodged against unknown vehicle.

Perusal of the criminal record produced before the Tribunal it is also found that the Marg was registered on the same date and Nakshapanchayatnama was done on 08.03.2019 in which the witnesses have stated that the death has occurred due to accident.
When police receives an information regarding the accident they registers it as Marg and enquire the matter.
In the present case the FIR was registered against unknown vehicle and after due investigation filed the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle.
The witness Suresh who was examined as eye witness in the present case is neither a relative or family member of the claimants.

He in his examination in chief has stated that on the date of accident he was going on his motorcycle and when he reached near Susner-Agar road Lolki waiting shed, he saw the offending vehicle bearing Cholamandalam Ms General Insurance vs Kanchanbai on 6 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154188548/
3 registration no.MP-70-G-0366 came rashly and negligently and hit the i-20 car and fled away.

sentences.text: In his cross examination in para-11 he has stated that he was not present when the police wrote Dehatinalishi.
He has not given any number of the offending vehicle to the police in the hospital.

Admittedly, Suresh was not a family member of the victim nor his friend, so he was not legally and morally liable to give the information of the registration number of the offending vehicle to the police.
8. After due investigation police trace out the offending vehicle and filed the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle.
However, the driver and owner of the offending vehicle did not dare to give any evidence in rebuttal to the criminal documents nor had dared to adduce any evidence before the Tribunal.
The owner and driver were present before the Tribunal till the disposal of the case but they had not dared to enter into the witness box to rebut the evidence of the claimants.
So a presumption can be drawn against the driver of the offending vehicle that he had caused the accident.

In view of the aforesaid discussion, in the considered opinion of this Court, the insurance company was unable to prove that the offending vehicle has been falsely implicated by the claimants for seeking compensation.
So this argument has no substance.
9. So far as quantum of compensation is concerned, in claim claim case no.57/2019 (MA No.2755/2022), the insurance company has not disputed the income of the deceased.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased as Rs.19,705/- per month.
So, the income of the deceased is fixed as Rs.19,705/- per month.

The deceased was 29 years of age at the time of accident, therefore,
future prospects must be added at the rate of 40%.

So the compensation amount is calculated as under:
 HEAD AMOUNT  Loss of dependency -Rs.28,13,874/-
 (i.e. Rs.19,705 40% F.P=27,587 x 12 x 17 - 1/2 )
 Consortium -Rs.80,000/-

Funeral expenses -Rs.15,000/-
 Loss of estate -Rs.15,000/-
 ----------------
. Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in M.A.No.2755/2022 is Rs.29,23,874/-.
Accordingly, the compensation amount in claim case no.57/2019 is reduced from Rs.36,47,838/- to Rs.29,23,874/-.
The said amount shall carry interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.

So, the income of the deceased is fixed as Rs.10,411/- per month.
The deceased was 28 years of age at the time of accident, therefore, future prospects must be added at the rate of 40%.

So the compensation amount is calculated as under:
 HEAD AMOUNT  Loss of dependency -Rs.14,86,650/
 (i.e. Rs.10,411 40% F.P=14,575 x 12 x 17 - 1/2)
 Consortium -Rs.80,000/-

Funeral expenses -Rs.15,000/-
 Loss of estate -Rs.15,000/-
 ----------------
12 . Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in M.A.No.2758/2022 is Rs.15,96,650/-.
Accordingly, the compensation amount in claim case no.56/2019 is reduced from Rs.19,41,463/- to Rs.15,96,650/-.
The said amount shall carry interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.
13. In the result, both the appeals are allowed in part and to the extent indicated herein above.
